question: A patient who has had a TIA or minor ischaemic stroke may resume driving a private vehicle immediately after discharge, provided their neurological deficits have resolved completely.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Symptom resolution does not mean the patient is immediately safe to drive. A mandatory restriction period applies post-TIA/stroke. This is an important counselling point as patients often incorrectly assume that complete symptom resolution equals unrestricted return to normal activities.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That statement is false. Even after complete clinical recovery from TIA or minor stroke, a mandatory driving restriction applies. In India, patients are generally advised not to drive for at least 4 weeks after TIA and 6 weeks after stroke, because of the risk of early stroke recurrence (highest in the first weeks) and possible residual cognitive effects not apparent on bedside examination.
